name: Giotto di Bondone
bio: Florentine painter who broke with Byzantine flatness and reintroduced naturalistic figures, spatial depth, and human emotion into Western painting. His Scrovegni Chapel frescoes mark the beginning of the Renaissance.

name: Jan van Eyck
bio: Flemish painter who perfected oil painting technique and brought unprecedented realism to portraiture and religious scenes. The Ghent Altarpiece and Arnolfini Portrait remain landmarks of Northern Renaissance art.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
bio: Italian polymath and painter whose studies of anatomy, light, engineering, and nature shaped the ideal of the Renaissance artist. His paintings are known for subtle modeling, psychological presence, and experimental composition.

name: Michelangelo Buonarroti
bio: Florentine sculptor, painter, architect, and poet. Michelangelo brought monumental anatomy and dramatic spiritual force to Renaissance art, from the Sistine Chapel ceiling to marble figures such as David.

name: Raphael
bio: Italian painter and architect celebrated for clarity, balanced composition, and graceful figures. Raphael's Vatican frescoes became defining examples of High Renaissance harmony.

name: Sandro Botticelli
bio: Florentine painter associated with lyrical line, mythological scenes, and refined devotional works. His Birth of Venus and Primavera helped define the poetic visual language of early Renaissance Florence.

name: Titian
bio: Venetian master whose rich color, loose handling, and confident portraiture influenced European painting for centuries. Titian's work bridged Renaissance ideals with a more sensual painterly approach.

name: Albrecht Dürer
bio: German painter, printmaker, and theorist who brought Italian Renaissance ideas north of the Alps. His woodcuts and engravings achieved unprecedented technical mastery and spread across Europe.

name: Hieronymus Bosch
bio: Dutch painter whose surreal, nightmarish visions of heaven and hell were centuries ahead of their time. The Garden of Earthly Delights remains one of the most enigmatic artworks ever created.

name: Caravaggio
bio: Revolutionary painter who brought dramatic chiaroscuro and gritty realism to sacred subjects. His intense lighting and visceral human figures changed the course of European painting.

name: Rembrandt van Rijn
bio: Dutch master of light, shadow, and human psychology. His portraits, self-portraits, and biblical scenes remain unmatched in their emotional depth and technical brilliance.

name: Johannes Vermeer
bio: Dutch painter famed for his serene domestic interiors bathed in cool northern light. His meticulous technique and quiet intimacy make every scene feel like a private moment frozen in time.

name: Peter Paul Rubens
bio: Flemish painter known for dynamic movement, lush color, and exuberant compositions. His large-scale altarpieces and mythological scenes defined the Baroque visual language.

name: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
bio: Sculptor, architect, and painter who gave marble the appearance of living flesh. His works in Rome, including the Ecstasy of Saint Teresa, embody Baroque theatricality.

name: Diego Velázquez
bio: Spanish court painter whose masterful brushwork and psychological depth made him one of the greatest portraitists in history. Las Meninas is a meditation on painting, reality, and royal power.

name: Artemisia Gentileschi
bio: One of the most accomplished Baroque painters and the first woman admitted to Florence's Accademia delle Arti del Disegno. Her powerful depictions of biblical heroines are marked by dramatic realism.

name: Caspar David Friedrich
bio: German Romantic painter whose misty landscapes and solitary wanderers evoke spiritual longing and the sublime power of nature. Wanderer above the Sea of Fog became an icon of Romanticism.

name: J. M. W. Turner
bio: British painter whose luminous, atmospheric seascapes and landscapes dissolved form into pure light and color. Turner paved the way for Impressionism and modern abstraction.

name: Eugène Delacroix
bio: French Romantic painter whose explosive color and energetic brushwork challenged the calm classicism of his era. Liberty Leading the People remains a symbol of revolutionary spirit.

name: Francisco Goya
bio: Spanish court painter who evolved from elegant Rococo portraits to dark, haunting visions of war, madness, and the supernatural. His Black Paintings and The Third of May 1808 are searing indictments of human cruelty.

name: Claude Monet
bio: French Impressionist who painted light itself rather than objects. His series of water lilies, haystacks, and Rouen Cathedral capture fleeting moments in vibrating color.

name: Vincent van Gogh
bio: Dutch painter whose bold, swirling brushstrokes and intense color expressed deep emotion. In just a decade he created some of the most recognizable images in art history.

name: Edgar Degas
bio: French painter and sculptor celebrated for his compositions of dancers, racehorses, and bathers. Degas combined classical draftsmanship with modern, off-center viewpoints.

name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
bio: French Impressionist painter of radiant light, warm flesh tones, and joyful social scenes. Renoir's touch remained gentle even as his style evolved toward classical form.

name: Paul Cézanne
bio: French painter who bridged Impressionism and Cubism. His methodical approach to form and color—building compositions with modulated planes—laid the foundation for 20th-century modern art.

name: Georges Seurat
bio: French painter who developed Pointillism—a scientific technique of applying tiny dots of pure color that blend in the viewer's eye. A Sunday Afternoon on La Grande Jatte is his masterpiece.

name: Gustav Klimt
bio: Austrian Symbolist painter whose gilded, decorative portraits and allegorical works defined Vienna's Golden Age. The Kiss remains one of the most beloved paintings in the world.

name: Pablo Picasso
bio: Spanish painter and sculptor who shattered perspective with Cubism. Picasso's restless experimentation across decades—from Blue Period to Guernica—made him the most influential artist of the 20th century.

name: Wassily Kandinsky
bio: Russian painter and theorist credited with creating the first purely abstract artworks. Kandinsky believed color and form could express spiritual truths without depicting reality.

name: Salvador Dalí
bio: Spanish Surrealist whose meticulously painted dreamscapes—melting clocks, burning giraffes—explored the unconscious mind with hallucinatory precision.

name: Frida Kahlo
bio: Mexican painter whose intensely personal self-portraits blended realism with symbolism, indigenous culture, and raw emotional honesty. Her work became a global icon of identity and resilience.

name: Henri Matisse
bio: French painter and sculptor who led Fauvism with explosive, non-naturalistic color. His later cut-out works—vibrant shapes of pure color—redefined what painting could be in old age.

name: Piet Mondrian
bio: Dutch painter who reduced art to its essentials: horizontal and vertical black lines, and primary colors on a white ground. His grid paintings influenced architecture, design, and fashion.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe
bio: American painter known as the 'Mother of American Modernism.' Her large-scale flower paintings, New York skyscrapers, and New Mexico landscapes transformed everyday subjects into iconic images.

name: Katsushika Hokusai
bio: Japanese ukiyo-e master whose woodblock prints—especially The Great Wave off Kanagawa—became some of the most recognized images in world art. His work profoundly influenced European Impressionists.

name: Utagawa Hiroshige
bio: Japanese ukiyo-e artist celebrated for his poetic landscape series, especially The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. His atmospheric scenes of rain, snow, and mist influenced Van Gogh and Monet.

name: Andy Warhol
bio: American artist who turned consumer products and celebrity faces into art. His Campbell's Soup Cans and Marilyn Monroe silkscreens blurred the line between high art and mass culture.

name: Jackson Pollock
bio: American painter who revolutionized art with his drip technique—pouring and splattering paint onto canvases laid on the floor. His 'action painting' made the creative process itself the subject.

name: Mark Rothko
bio: American painter whose large, luminous rectangles of color were designed to envelop the viewer in a meditative, almost spiritual experience. His works are meant to be encountered, not just seen.

name: Yayoi Kusama
bio: Japanese artist whose immersive Infinity Mirror Rooms and obsessive polka-dot patterns explore themes of repetition, infinity, and self-obliteration. One of the most popular living artists worldwide.

name: Banksy
bio: Anonymous British street artist whose stenciled works combine dark humor with political commentary. From shredding a painting at auction to painting on the West Bank barrier, Banksy redefined what art can be.

name: Gerhard Richter
bio: German painter who moves effortlessly between photorealism and abstraction. His blurred photo-paintings and squeegeed abstract canvases make him one of the most important living artists.

name: Edward Hopper
bio: American realist painter whose scenes of urban loneliness—diners at night, solitary figures in sunlit rooms—captured the quiet isolation of modern American life. Nighthawks is his most iconic work.

name: René Magritte
bio: Belgian Surrealist who challenged perceptions of reality with deadpan wit. A pipe labeled 'This is not a pipe' and men in bowler hats with apples obscuring their faces became icons of philosophical art.

name: Edvard Munch
bio: Norwegian painter whose intensely psychological works explored anxiety, love, and death. The Scream became one of the most recognizable images in art history—a universal symbol of existential dread.

name: David Hockney
bio: British artist whose vibrant California pool paintings, double portraits, and recent iPad landscapes span six decades of restless innovation. One of the most influential British artists of the 20th century.

name: Jean-Michel Basquiat
bio: American artist who rose from graffiti on New York streets to international fame. His raw, text-laden paintings addressed race, power, and identity with explosive energy before his death at 27.
